baseline_source.commit_subject: docs: spec, plan, and tasks for concurrency & robustness hardening
baseline_source.why_not_main_tip: The requested target branch was main, but this feature's three implementation commits (f086cfa, 7ea3e66, 8feb989) are already merged into main — main's tip at 1de1eb0 IS the post-change state. Capturing it and filing it as before/ would have produced images that are pre-change in name only. 2ec8788 is the last commit before the first implementation commit, so it is the true pre-change tree. Judgement call made unattended and recorded here rather than asked.
baseline_source.how: git worktree add --detach /tmp/sc-baseline 2ec8788, node_modules symlinked from the main checkout (package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are unchanged between 2ec8788 and main), CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointed at the main checkout's src-tauri/target so only the site-checker crate recompiled. Worktree removed after the run; no repo file outside screenshots/ was touched.
baseline_source.frontend_identity_check: git diff 2ec8788..main -- src index.html src-tauri/tauri.conf.json is EMPTY, and diff -r on src/ confirms byte identity. The baseline and the implementation share the same frontend exactly; only the five Rust files differ. Any pixel difference between before/ and after/ therefore comes from Rust-produced strings or from capture conditions, never from frontend edits.

seed_rationale: The skill's dependable default (one reachable site, one .invalid that never resolves so Down renders without waiting on a real outage) plus a third unlabelled site, because render.ts shows label-or-URL per row and the feature's evidence is about which rows exist. method_override is omitted deliberately: model.rs marks it #[serde(default)], so the seed parses without it. The before run reused this list verbatim from the manifest, which is what makes the two passes comparable.

views.why: The populated list plus the add form. Reference for FR-009/FR-012 and SC-003 — after the change, a refused add must produce zero rows, so the after run compares row-for-row against this.
views.how_to_reach: Launch with the seed above; wait ~10s for Pending to resolve to Up/Down.
views.before_observation: All three seed rows render with resolved statuses — Example: Up, Never Up: Down, https://example.org: Up. The unlabelled third site falls back to its URL as the row title. At 480x320 the Add button wraps below the input row and the 'Launch at login' footer clips at the window floor. Every one of these traits is already present before the change, which is what makes them pre-existing layout rather than something this feature introduced.
views.after_observation: All three seed rows render with resolved statuses — Example: Up, Never Up: Down, https://example.org: Up. The unlabelled third site falls back to its URL as the row title, unchanged. At 480x320 the Add button wraps below the input row and the 'Launch at login' footer clips at the window floor; that is the pre-existing layout at the minimum size, not something this feature introduced.

views.why: The add form with an error showing in #site-error. FR-010 rewords exactly this message — form.ts:101 renders a Rust Err(String) here — so the baseline pins today's wording and placement.
views.how_to_reach: Type an invalid URL (e.g. 'ftp://example.com') into #site-url and submit. NOTE: the FR-010 duplicate-id refusal itself is NOT reachable by clicking, on either branch — every add mints a fresh id (spec Assumptions). Both passes capture this same invalid-URL error for a like-for-like comparison and rely on the automated tests (T019/T020/T023/T024) for the refusal string itself.
views.before_observation: Submitting 'ftp://example.com' renders 'Only http and https URLs are supported' in #site-error, the row count stays at three, and sites.json was verified byte-identical (sha1 unchanged) across the refused add. The pre-change code already refuses this input cleanly and already leaves the file alone — so FR-009/FR-012 are confirmed here as no-regressions rather than as new behaviour on the reachable path.
views.after_observation: Submitting 'ftp://example.com' renders 'Only http and https URLs are supported' in #site-error and the row count stays at three — the refused add added no row (FR-009) and left sites.json untouched (FR-012, verified by re-reading the seed file after the submit). This is the reachable-by-clicking rejection path; the duplicate-id refusal string that FR-010 actually rewords remains unreachable from the UI on both branches, exactly as the before pass predicted, and stays covered by the automated tests.

views.why: The #banner element visible. FR-004 raises the new poison-recovery warning through this same banner rather than a new mechanism, so the baseline shows the banner the after run must match.
views.how_to_reach: Write an unparseable sites.json (e.g. '{') before launch; the store load failure surfaces in #banner with the empty state below it. Restore the seed afterwards.
views.before_observation: The banner reads 'sites.json is not valid JSON (invalid type: map, expected a sequence at line 1 column 0). Starting with an empty list; the existing file has been left alone.' with the empty state below it — the identical string the after pass shows. The banner wraps to three lines at 480x320 and pushes the rest of the layout down without overflow, before the change as well as after.
views.after_observation: The banner reads 'sites.json is not valid JSON (invalid type: map, expected a sequence at line 1 column 0). Starting with an empty list; the existing file has been left alone.' with the empty state below it. This is store.rs's load-failure message, not FR-004's poison-recovery message — the latter needs a genuinely poisoned lock, which no sequence of clicks can produce. What this shot demonstrates is the mechanism FR-004 reuses: the same #banner element, same placement, same styling, so the poison warning will surface here rather than through anything new. The banner wraps to three lines at 480x320 and still pushes the rest of the layout down without overflow.

comparison.method: Per-pixel RGB comparison of each before/after pair at tolerance 12/255, reporting the count of differing pixels and their bounding box. Run from the same compiled helper used for capture.
comparison.interpretation: The two warning-banner pairs are pixel-identical, which is the strongest single piece of evidence in this set: the banner mechanism FR-004 reuses renders byte-for-byte the same before and after. The four non-zero pairs differ only in (a) the 'LAST CHECKED' relative-time text, which is wall-clock dependent and cannot match across two runs taken 90 minutes apart, and (b) on site-list-default only, macOS window-active chrome — the after capture caught the window inactive (grey traffic lights, grey 'Launch at login' checkbox) while the baseline capture had it frontmost, which is what stretches that bbox to y9 and y460. No row, column, control, label, status dot, or error string moved or changed. That is the expected result: plan.md said zero frontend files change, and the frontend_identity_check above proves it independently.

ui_relevance.reasoning: plan.md states zero frontend files change and src/ is untouched. But the skill's exception for backend work that changes user-visible output applies: FR-004 adds a new store-warning banner message, FR-010 rewords the refused-add message the user reads (it must stop implying the change is merely unsaved), and FR-009 removes a row that appears today. Those are user-visible output changes, so this was NOT treated as a skip.

This is why the manifest previously recorded baseline: unavailable.

notes: A true before/after pair now exists for all three views. The previous manifest recorded baseline: unavailable and asked for exactly this — 're-run the before pass against the merge-base from a session like this one' — which is what this run did.

Both branches build and start cleanly. The base branch is NOT broken: 2ec8788 compiled in 9.07s against the shared cargo target dir and launched twice without error, so the unattended-run instruction about reporting a broken base does not apply.
Feature resolved from .specify/feature.json in the primary checkout, which this time points at the correct feature (specs/20260806-120353-concurrency-hardening).

add-error-narrow was captured twice: the first attempt lost focus between the resize and the grab, producing inactive window chrome and an unfocused input ring that would not have matched its after counterpart. It was re-captured with the window frontmost and the field focused. Only the second capture was kept.

The duplicate-id refusal (FR-010) and the poison-recovery warning (FR-004) are still not reachable by clicking on either branch, exactly as the original pass predicted — every add mints a fresh id, and no sequence of clicks poisons a lock. Those two strings remain covered by the automated tests, not by these images.

The user's real sites.json was moved to sites.json.shots-backup and additionally copied out of tree to /tmp/site-checker-sites-SAFETY-before-run-20260806.json before seeding. It was restored at the end and verified with both sha1 (7150bef89871c83ceb3b9064e67b8ac1e499ee56, unchanged) and a full diff against the safety copy. The dev process tree was launched into its own process group (perl setpgrp) and torn down with kill -TERM/-KILL on the group; no site-checker or vite process survived and port 1420 was confirmed free before the restore.
The /tmp/sc-baseline worktree was removed and pruned. Nothing outside FEATURE_DIR/screenshots/ was modified in the repo, and no dev-server log or data file was committed.
